correctness.rationale: The rowwise negative bound q_i<=i-1 follows from binary vertical prefixes and preceding row-end sums; unit norms <=m^2 and negative-products >=-m(m-1) imply squared diameter <=2m(2m-1). Equality forces full negativity budgets, unit row sums and pairwise opposite-sign matching. The two unmatched final-row positives enforce 2m distinct staggered columns; interlaced previous-row states determine the whole pair uniquely. Every constructed pair meets both prefix constraints and the exact distance; counting selected columns and transpose symmetry completes the statement. The supplementary checker confirms exhaustive low sizes and 1,626 constructions, without substituting for the proof.

value.rationale: The statement determines a natural global metric invariant over the full two-parameter signed-matrix polytope family up to a sharp saturated regime and counts every farthest pair. The 2s aspect-ratio cutoff and forced 2s-column alternating diamonds are structural geometric phenomena, not tiny numerical gains or routine tabulation. Squared signed-matrix diameter grows quadratically in the short dimension compared with linear scale for the contained ordinary partial permutation matrices, motivating its study.
